sources_considered.why: Preprint by Sun Yat-sen University and Alibaba. It summarizes the classic literature on maintenance cost and Lehman's laws and reports agent results.
Primary Lehman paper stating the Increasing Complexity law. The two-column table text was too jumbled to quote reliably.
Program comprehension study (58% of developer time). It is indirect, its text extraction is jumbled, and it reports that project age has limited effect on comprehension time.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv (Chen et al., Sun Yat-sen University and Alibaba Group)

receipt.public_excerpt: Lehman’s Laws reveal that software quality inherently degrades as maintenance progresses [7], while classic literature has established that maintenance activities account for 60% to 80% of total software lifecycle costs [2].

evidence_items.explanation: Summarizes established software-engineering findings: maintenance is most of lifecycle cost, and quality degrades as maintenance goes on. This fits the plain reading that long-term maintenance is the larger, harder task.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv (Chen et al., Sun Yat-sen University and Alibaba Group)

receipt.public_excerpt: although LLMs have shown significant improvements in snapshot-based code modification tasks, they still face substantial challenges in fully automated, long-term, and multi-round software development and maintenance scenarios.

evidence_items.explanation: For AI agents, long-term maintenance proved harder than one-shot code changes. This fits the claim but concerns AI, not coders in general, so it is context only.

unresolved_gaps: I could not quote a primary source for the 60-80% maintenance cost figure (Brooks, Lientz and Swanson). It comes through a 2026 preprint's summary.
Cost share is not the same as per-task difficulty. No direct measurement of 'harder' was found.
No survey shows what competent coders believe.
